package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious file, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: Donbass.ppam is a malicious PowerPoint add-in containing a macro that stages and decodes a secondary payload, establishes persistence via scheduled tasks, and exfiltrates system information to a remote C2 server. Its behavior matches known Konni RAT delivery techniques, including covert payload staging, abuse of system utilities, persistent execution, and unauthorized network communication.

execution_context.trigger: When the user opens Donbass.ppam in PowerPoint, triggering macro execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The macro presents a message box to the user, then writes a large block of base64-encoded text to a file named 'oup.dat' in the user's %TMP% directory.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon macro execution, the code displays a message box to the user, writes a base64-encoded payload to %TMP%\oup.dat, staging a secondary payload for subsequent decoding and execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that write encoded payloads to disk are commonly used to stage malware while evading static detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Office add-ins do not write encoded payloads to temporary directories without explicit user action or clear business justification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may extract encoded files for self-extraction, but this is not standard or expected in Office macro code.
key_indicators: No user interaction required beyond opening the add-in
Message box used as social engineering or execution marker

execution_context.trigger: Immediately after snippet_1, during the same macro execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The macro uses the Microsoft 'certutil' command-line tool to decode the base64-encoded 'oup.dat' file, producing 'oup.vbs' in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After staging the encoded payload, the macro invokes certutil.exe to decode %TMP%\oup.dat, writing the decoded VBScript as %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office\oup.vbs, preparing the malicious script for persistent execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of certutil.exe to decode and drop payloads is a well-documented malware tactic to bypass detection and leverage trusted system utilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Office add-ins should not invoke system tools like certutil to decode files or drop scripts into Office application directories.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of certutil for decoding is rare in Office automation and almost never performed by macros.
key_indicators: Invocation of certutil.exe from macro code
Decoding of base64 file to produce a script

execution_context.trigger: Immediately after snippet_2, during the same macro execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The macro creates a scheduled task named 'Office Updatev2.2' that runs 'oup.vbs' from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office every 5 minutes.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During macro execution, the code uses schtasks.exe to create a scheduled task named 'Office Updatev2.2' that executes %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office\oup.vbs every 5 minutes, establishing persistent execution of the malicious script.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware frequently uses scheduled tasks to maintain persistence and ensure repeated execution of payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Office add-ins are not expected to create persistent scheduled tasks, especially those that execute scripts from Office directories.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate updaters may use scheduled tasks, but not via Office macros or for scripts placed in Office directories.

execution_context.trigger: Each time the scheduled task 'Office Updatev2.2' runs (every 5 minutes)
required_permissions: network (to connect to external C2 server)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: oup.vbs executes a base64-encoded PowerShell command that collects environment information such as the machine name and user name, then connects to gg1593.c1.biz (185.176.43.106) to exfiltrate the data.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On each scheduled execution, oup.vbs runs a base64-encoded PowerShell command that gathers system environment details and sends them to the remote C2 server at gg1593.c1.biz (185.176.43.106), resulting in unauthorized exfiltration of host information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated collection and exfiltration of system information to an external server is a hallmark of remote access trojans and initial access malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Office add-ins should never exfiltrate data or communicate with external C2 infrastructure, especially via hidden scripts and scheduled tasks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or inventory tools may collect system info, but not via hidden scripts deployed by Office macros and not to suspicious external domains.
key_indicators: Execution of base64-encoded PowerShell from VBScript
Exfiltration of environment and system information

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious Donbass.ppam PowerPoint add-in, triggering macro execution that writes a base64-encoded payload to %TMP%\oup.dat.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload staging in the temporary directory

attack_chain.action: Macro decodes the staged payload using certutil.exe, dropping oup.vbs in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious VBScript is prepared for execution

attack_chain.action: Macro creates a scheduled task named 'Office Updatev2.2' to run oup.vbs every 5 minutes, establishing persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent execution of the malicious script

attack_chain.action: oup.vbs executes a base64-encoded PowerShell command to collect system information and exfiltrate it to the C2 server at gg1593.c1.biz (185.176.43.106).
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of environment data and potential further payload delivery

behavioral_signatures: Office macro writes base64-encoded files (e.g., oup.dat) to %TMP%
Macro invokes certutil.exe to decode files dropped by Office macros
Creation of scheduled tasks (e.g., 'Office Updatev2.2') by Office processes
Outbound network connections to gg1593.c1.biz or 185.176.43.106 from scheduled scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office macros that write base64-encoded files to disk and invoke certutil.exe for decoding. Alert on creation of scheduled tasks by Office processes, especially those executing scripts from Office directories. Detect execution of PowerShell or VBScript from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office. Monitor for outbound connections to gg1593.c1.biz or 185.176.43.106. Correlate these behaviors for high-confidence detection of this attack chain.
